question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}(4-x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<2 \\ h(x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1,\, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2\le x\le 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ {\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{2}^{x}\frac{2}{3}(4-t)\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={-\frac{1}{3}t(t-8)|}_{2}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}x(x-8)-4 \\  & =\frac{-{x}^{2}+8x-12}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ \frac{-{x}^{2}+8x-12}{3}, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$
